title: The Hour That Happens Twice: Why Clock Changes Break Software
topic: Daylight saving time / time zones in code
audience: Junior devs, anyone whose calendar invite shifted by an hour
whyCare: Europe falls back on Sun Oct 25 2026 and the US on Nov 1, so 01:30 happens twice and Europe-US meetings shift for a week. Timely, relatable bug.

evidence.claim: European clocks go back on Sunday 25 October 2026; the US changes on 1 November 2026, so the transatlantic offset differs for about a week
UK: British Summer Time ends 25 Oct 2026, clocks go from 2am back to 1am
Low competition: 'Your Code Works. It Just Breaks Twice a Year.' 3,271 views (1 month); Short 'Why 2:30 AM Can Disappear in Code' 474 views

angle: Timeline scene: 00:59 -> 01:00 -> 01:59 -> 01:00 again (strike + repeat). A nightly job fires twice (packet x2). Compare table: local time vs UTC. Rule card: store UTC, convert at the edge.
hook: This Sunday, 1:30 AM will happen twice. Your code might run twice too.
